title: Frontmatter of an imported KB entry
description: Lands at kb/external/bd/<id>.md (AM side) or knowledge/external/am/<id>.md (BD side). Path carries the foreign origin so a citation is self-describing; a frontmatter field alone is not enough, because AM plans cite by path.

source_hash.description: Checked by the importing repo's own check CLI. Upstream drift flags every plan citing this entry.

evidence_class.description: Surfaced at citation time. A simulated f_c must never sit in kb/calibrations/, which means 'measured on this instrument'. When `evidence_classes` is present this must equal the worst class in it, by the severity order measured = handbook < computed < simulated = round_trip < assumed. Checked by R10.

may_be_gate_threshold.description: false for everything imported by default. A gate that clears against a simulated threshold emits a margin that looks measured -- the disease AM hard rule 3 already names.

superseded_by.description: Lifecycle is supersession, not deletion. A deleted import dangles every decision that cited it.

question.description: The question this import answers, in one line. Optional here because it is not part of the handoff -- but AM's knowledge/index.py requires it of every indexed entry, and an imported number absent from kb/INDEX.md is one nobody finds. Each repository enforces its own requirement; the wire only has to stop forbidding it.

date.description: Index metadata for the importing repository, same reason as `question`. Distinct from `imported`: `date` is the entry's own date in its KB, `imported` is when it crossed.

evidence_classes.description: Per-value evidence, keyed by symbol. The mixed case is the NORMAL case: r1's import carries d and pixel_size (genuinely measured) alongside T (assumed, AM's own P3 blocks on a thermometer), eta (computed from that assumed T) and k_t (a model output). A single top-level class either lies or throws away the fact that two of them really are measurements. When this is present, `evidence_class` MUST be the worst entry in it (rule R10) -- so a citation can never read better than the entry's weakest number.
